results.name: Plate Overhead Press to Tricep Extension
instructions: Hold a weight plate at your chest and press it overhead.
With your upper arms by your ears, lower the plate behind your head by bending your elbows.
Extend your elbows to bring the plate back overhead.
Lower the plate to your chest and repeat.
tips: Keep your elbows pointing forward during the extension.
Brace your core.
results.description: Plate Overhead Press to Tricep Extension is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core.

results.name: Plate Overhead Shrug
instructions: Press a weight plate overhead with your arms locked out.
Shrug your shoulders up toward your ears, pushing the plate higher.
Hold briefly.
Lower your shoulders with control and repeat.
tips: Keep your arms locked.
Good for overhead stability.
results.description: Plate Overhead Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Serratus Anterior.

results.name: Plate Reach
instructions: Stand holding a weight plate at your chest.
Press the plate straight out in front of you.
Hold it briefly at arm's length.
Bring it back to your chest and repeat.
tips: Keep your core braced.
Don't let your shoulders shrug.
results.description: Plate Reach is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Chest.

results.name: Plate Rear Delt Fly
instructions: Hinge forward with a flat back, holding a light plate in each hand.
Let your arms hang below your shoulders with a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms out to the sides until they are level with your shoulders.
Lower slowly and repeat.
tips: Keep your neck in line with your spine.
Use a light weight.
results.description: Plate Rear Delt Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Traps.

results.name: Prone Front Raises Barbell on Bench
instructions: Lie chest-first on an incline bench, holding a barbell with both hands using a pronated grip (palms facing down) and a shoulder-width hand placement. Your arms should be extended straight down towards the floor.
Lift the barbell straight up in front of you until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your body pressed firmly against the bench to prevent lower back strain.
Focus on lifting with your shoulders and not your arms to maximize shoulder engagement.
Exhale as you lift the barbell and inhale as you lower it.
results.description: Prone Front Raises Barbell on Bench is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest, Upper Back.

results.name: Prone Front Raises Dumbbell on Bench
instructions: Lie chest-first on an incline bench, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip (palms facing down). Your arms should be extended straight down towards the floor.
Raise the dumbbells straight up in front of you until your arms are in line with your torso.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Keep your body pressed firmly against the bench to prevent lower back strain.
Focus on lifting with your shoulders and not your arms to maximize shoulder engagement.
Exhale as you lift the barbell and inhale as you lower it.
results.description: Prone Front Raises Dumbbell on Bench is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Pull Apart Cable Resistance Band
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a resistance band with both hands, arms extended straight in front of you at shoulder height. Your palms should be facing the floor.
Pull the resistance band apart by moving your arms out to your sides.
Slowly return your arms to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your arms straight throughout the exercise, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows to avoid locking them.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce injury risk.
Exhale as you pull the band apart and inhale as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Pull Apart Cable Resistance Band is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

results.name: Reaching Up Shoulder Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your right elbow and bring your right arm behind your back, raising your hand upward with your palm facing out.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly release and return to the starting position. Repeat on the other side by bending your left elbow and using your right hand to assist with the stretch.
tips: Move slowly and with control to avoid any sudden movements that could cause strain.
Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and support your lower back.
Avoid arching your back; keep your spine neutral to maximize the stretch and prevent injury.
results.description: Reaching Up Shoulder Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Rear Deltoid Fly Cable Resistance Band
instructions: Attach the resistance band to a shoulder height anchor point in front of you. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the handles with both hands, arms extended straight in front of you at shoulder height, palms facing each other.
Pull the handles out to your sides by extending your arms and squeezing your shoulder blades together, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly return your arms to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you pull the handles apart and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Use a lighter resistance band if needed to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Focus on engaging your rear deltoid and upper back muscles throughout the movement.
results.description: Rear Deltoid Fly Cable Resistance Band is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Triceps.

results.name: Resistance Band Face Pull
instructions: Attach a resistance band to an anchor point at face height. Stand facing the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with both hands, palms facing down.
Step back to create tension in the band and extend your arms straight in front of you at shoulder height.
Pull the handles towards your face by bending your elbows and spreading them out to the sides, keeping your upper arms parallel to the floor.
Slowly return to the starting position with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you pull the handles towards your face and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Use a lighter resistance band if needed to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Focus on engaging your upper back and rear shoulders throughout the movement.
results.description: Resistance Band Face Pull is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms.
